business_problem: Last Mile Health found that medical and community health advice delivered through Ethiopia's new health-system call centers was not standardized across districts, while community health workers could not realistically memorize hundreds of pages of guidelines, training content, and diagnostic protocols for unusual cases.
solution_summary: Last Mile Health, working with the Ethiopian Ministry of Health and technical partner IDinsight, created HEP Assist to support community health workers through 10 call centers embedded in Ethiopia's health system. The implementation combines HEP Assist with a case management system and a question-answering service trained on Ethiopian Ministry of Health guidelines, training materials, and diagnostic protocols. In the current operating model, frontline workers call center agents when they encounter unusual symptoms or difficult cases. Agents then use the AI to connect symptom lists, surface standardized medical guidance, and determine whether a patient should be referred for specialized or emergency care. Ministry experts guided the design, and the rollout is structured as an agent-mediated pilot first, with longer-term plans for direct access via mobile devices. The source does not name the underlying model, storage platform, or cloud infrastructure.

solution_components.name: HEP Assist
solution_components.role: Provides real-time medical guidance and referral support for Ethiopian health workers through the call center workflow.

solution_components.name: case management system
solution_components.role: Supports handling of incoming cases as the pilot operates across the 10 health-system call centers.

solution_components.name: question-answering service
solution_components.role: Answers agent questions using Ethiopian Ministry of Health guidelines, training content, and diagnostic protocols.

data_flow: Community health workers call center agents with symptom descriptions or difficult cases; agents submit those questions to HEP Assist and its question-answering service, which uses Ethiopian Ministry of Health guidelines, training content, and diagnostic protocols to return standardized guidance and referral recommendations, including when to escalate patients to nearby health facilities.
integration_points: Ethiopian Ministry of Health training content
Ethiopian Ministry of Health diagnostic protocols
10 local call centers embedded within Ethiopia's health system
Nearby health facilities for specialized or emergency referrals
business_outcome: The initiative is intended to standardize medical guidance across districts, help community health workers deliver better care, support faster and more appropriate referrals, improve efficiency for call center agents, and reduce unnecessary strain and costs in hospital systems.
